decision: Use an atomic local JSON snapshot store guarded by an atomic mkdir lock for the first durable worker milestone

evaluatedApproaches.name: atomic-json-plus-lockdir
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: high for multiple local processes sharing one filesystem; claim/update mutations are serialized
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: good for process restarts and stale locks; atomic rename prevents partial snapshots
evaluatedApproaches.latency: good for current small queue sizes; whole-state JSON rewrite is O(n)
evaluatedApproaches.resourceUse: low; no external service or dependency
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: low-to-medium because it is introduced as a separate DurableMissionQueue rather than replacing the in-memory queue
evaluatedApproaches.qa: 4 focused tests pass: restart persistence, concurrent atomic claim, lease recovery, dependency gating

evaluatedApproaches.name: sqlite
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: strong on one host, but adds runtime/version/dependency questions not represented in the current package
evaluatedApproaches.latency: likely better at larger queue sizes
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: medium because it changes runtime assumptions and requires an additional integration surface

evaluatedApproaches.name: external-coordinator-db
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: best path for truly distributed multi-host workers
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: high for the current lab because it introduces a service dependency before worker protocol/authentication is finalized
evaluatedApproaches.qa: deferred until Qubes worker transport and authentication exist

whyItWon: It closes the immediate restart-loss and duplicate local-claim gaps with minimal dependencies and preserves the existing queue implementation for fallback. It is the strongest risk-adjusted lab step before introducing a real distributed coordinator.
knownFailuresAndLessons: The store is not a real multi-host distributed database; workers must share the same filesystem for the lock to coordinate them.
Whole-state JSON rewrites will become a throughput bottleneck as mission volume grows.
Stale-lock recovery is time-based and cannot by itself prove that a remote worker is dead.
Before REAL-WORKER READY, add worker authentication, fenced lease tokens, fault-injection stress tests, and a coordinator suitable for separate Qubes VMs.
